phrases.syllabary_text: ᎬᎵᎡᎵᏥᏏ ᏥᎷᎦ

phrases.phonetic_broad: kvlelitsis tsiluka
phrases.english_text: I am glad that you came here.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: OK.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎬᏱ ᎨᎲ ᎬᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᏰᎸᏛ ᏥᏂᎾᏛᏁᎠ ᏣᎾᏔᏅ ᏓᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎠᎭᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: vkvyi kehv kvnohihsi nuyelhvtv tsini'ntvne'a tsanthnv tanatelhohkwahsk tiniyolhi ahana
phrases.phonetic_broad: vkvyi kev kvnoisi nuyelvtv tsinintvnea tsantnv tanatelokwask tiniyoli aana
phrases.english_text: First let me tell you the reason we are doing this. You know that kids are going to school here?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yeah.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏢᏴ ᏛᎾᎴᏂ ᎠᎾᏛᏓᏍᏗᎲ Ꭿ ᏥᏂᏬᏂ ᏓᏂᏬᏂᏏ Ꮥ
phrases.phonetic_text: skitv lhvy tvnleni anthvtahstihv hi tsiniwoni taniwonihs te
phrases.phonetic_broad: skitv lvy tvnleni antvtastiv i tsiniwoni taniwonis te
phrases.english_text: One of these days they are going to start listening to us, talking how we are. Or we are going to be talking, [for them] to listen to how Cherokee is spoken. I don’t know if they are going to get that far—but the reason is for them to listen. And, also, your grandchildren or your immediate family might want to someday listen to you talking. If they come here and ask, they will let them listen to you talking, or us talking. As we begin, tell me your full name in English.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮩ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏝᏅ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ ᏍᎩ Ᏼ ᏳᏛᏅᏟᎶᏝ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᎤᏰᎵᏗ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: unthvtahstohti nuhstv to tsalak kawonihihst kehv tlnv ywanvhth ski yv ytvntlhilola ahsenv unthvtahstohti uyelhit kehsehsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: untvtastoti nustv to tsalak kawoniist kev tlnv ywanvt ski yv ytvntlilola asenv untvtastoti uyelit kesesti
phrases.english_text: One of these days they are going to start listening to us, talking how we are. Or we are going to be talking, [for them] to listen to how Cherokee is spoken. I don’t know if they are going to get that far—but the reason is for them to listen. And, also, your grandchildren or your immediate family might want to someday listen to you talking. If they come here and ask, they will let them listen to you talking, or us talking. As we begin, tell me your full name in English.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᎢᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎢᏣᏙᏢᏒ ᏢᏴ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᎤᏅᏛᎪᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: so'in kehv tiketsalihs sitanelv itsatolhvhsv lhvy yuntuli kehehsti unthvkoti hiwonihskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: soin kev tiketsalis sitanelv itsatolvsv lvy yuntuli keesti untvkoti iwoniskv
phrases.english_text: One of these days they are going to start listening to us, talking how we are. Or we are going to be talking, [for them] to listen to how Cherokee is spoken. I don’t know if they are going to get that far—but the reason is for them to listen. And, also, your grandchildren or your immediate family might want to someday listen to you talking. If they come here and ask, they will let them listen to you talking, or us talking. As we begin, tell me your full name in English.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏅ ᏳᎾᏓᏙᎮᎵᏝ ᎨᏒ ᏴᎨᎬᎵᏍᎪᎳᏓᏏ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎢᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎴᏱᎩ ᎨᏒ ᎯᎢᎾᎾ ᎢᎾᎴᏂᏍᎬ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᎧᎵ ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinv yunatatohelil kehsv ykekvlihskohltahs kehehsti untvtahstohti hiwonihskv iniwonihskv lyik kehs hi'inna inlenihskv yonek kvt khali tetsato'v skhinohihsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinv yunatatoelil kesv ykekvliskoltas keesti untvtastoti iwoniskv iniwoniskv lyik kes iinna inleniskv yonek kvt kali tetsatov skinoisi
phrases.english_text: One of these days they are going to start listening to us, talking how we are. Or we are going to be talking, [for them] to listen to how Cherokee is spoken. I don’t know if they are going to get that far—but the reason is for them to listen. And, also, your grandchildren or your immediate family might want to someday listen to you talking. If they come here and ask, they will let them listen to you talking, or us talking. As we begin, tell me your full name in English.

phrases.phonetic_broad: tsiskw waya
phrases.english_text: Tsisqwe Wahaya.

phrases.phonetic_broad: tsiskw waya alv tsatenv

phrases.syllabary_text: Rocky Mountain Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: wakhi mantan tv awatenhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: waki mantan tv awatenv
phrases.english_text: I was born in Rocky Mountain.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎾᏭᏍ ᏗᏤᏅᎲᏭᏍ ᏣᏕᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: unawhs ttsenvhvwuhs tstene
phrases.phonetic_broad: unaws ttsenvvwus tstene
phrases.english_text: So, you were born just there, at your home?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏗᏪᏅᏒᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tiwenvhsvwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tiwenvsvwu
phrases.english_text: At my house.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕ ᎤᎾ ᏅᏱ ᎣᏓᎳ
phrases.phonetic_text: to uhste una nvyi otala
phrases.phonetic_broad: to uste una nvyi otala
phrases.english_text: What was it like there at Rocky Mountain?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎦᏛ ᎤᏛᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ ᏞᏍᏗ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏱᏄᏍᏓ ᏃᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: ikatv utnetliyvhs khohiy tsiki lhst tsinuhstv ynuhst nhole
phrases.phonetic_broad: ikatv utnetliyvs koiy tsiki lst tsinustv ynust nole
phrases.english_text: It has really changed nowadays. It is not like it was. Also, there are three mountains. On this side, Rocky Mountain, they call it and on this side Jackson Mountain. I grew up that way. You know where they call Mankiller Flats?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏦᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏓᎵ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏝ ᏅᏱ ᎣᏓᎳ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏝ Jackson Mountain ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏝ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ ᏣᎾᏛ Ꮎ Mankiller flats ᏣᏃᏎᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: tso'i hen totali hi'i tila nvyi otal tsanohsho hi'i til tsakhhsan mantan anhseho un heni tila awathvhsv tsanhat na mankhiwa swaths tsanohsho
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsoi en totali ii tila nvyi otal tsanoso ii til tsaksan mantan anseo un eni tila awatvsv tsanat na mankiwa swats tsanoso
phrases.english_text: It has really changed nowadays. It is not like it was. Also, there are three mountains. On this side, Rocky Mountain, they call it and on this side Jackson Mountain. I grew up that way. You know where they call Mankiller Flats?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yes.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᎤ ᏗᏝ ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏗᏝ
phrases.phonetic_text: hi'u tila ukanaw tila
phrases.phonetic_broad: iu tila ukanaw tila
phrases.english_text: That way, to the south.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᎭᎳᎩ ᏂᏥᎡ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: o halak nitsi'e sitanelv
phrases.phonetic_broad: o alak nitsie sitanelv
phrases.english_text: Oh. How many was in your family?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎯᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᏃᏥᎥ ᎣᏥᏧᏥ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣᏅ ᏦᎢ
phrases.phonetic_text: hihsktv tsnotsi'v otsitshutsi anikyhutsan tso'i
phrases.phonetic_broad: isktv tsnotsiv otsitsutsi anikyutsan tsoi

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏗᎨ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikatkhe tsalaki itsiwonihsk kehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikatke tsalaki itsiwonisk kee
phrases.english_text: Did you all speak Cherokee?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓᏛ ᎣᏥᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikatahtv otsitsalk kvti otsiwonihsk kehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikatatv otsitsalk kvti otsiwonisk kev
phrases.english_text: All of us spoke Cherokee.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏅ ᎤᏍᏕ ᎤᎾ ᏙᏗᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ Ꮎ ᏛᎬᏁᏟᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏥᏄᏍᏗ ᏧᏂᎾ ᎪᎯ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏂᎾ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎢᏥᎾᎡᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tonv uhste un totitsathvhsitihsv na tkvneltti khuhst tsnuhst tsuninha khohi tiniyol nina to uhsti itsina'ewu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tonv uste un totitsatvsitisv na tkvneltti kust tsnust tsunina koi tiniyol nina to usti itsinaewu
phrases.english_text: What was it like for you growing up? The things you could play with compared to what children have today. What did you all have?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᏭᏛ ᎣᏦᏢᏍᎬᏭ ᏦᎦᏁᎵᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: nwtv otsolhvhskvw tskanelhitoht khuhst
phrases.phonetic_broad: nwtv otsolvskvw tskanelitot kust
phrases.english_text: We just made things to play with. And just down the hill there was a big creek where we had a place to swim. We would clean it out.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏃᎴ ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎨᏓᎵ ᏗᏝ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎣᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᎣᎪᏢᏒ ᎣᎩᏅᎦᎸᎰ ᏂᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: nle hi'i nuhstv khetl tila uweyv uthani okatawohsti okolhsv okinvkalvho nkehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: nle ii nustv ketl tila uweyv utani okatawosti okolsv okinvkalvo nkev
phrases.english_text: We just made things to play with. And just down the hill there was a big creek where we had a place to swim. We would clean it out.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎾᏭᏅ ᎢᏤᏙᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: unawunv itsetohe
phrases.phonetic_broad: unawunv itsetoe
phrases.english_text: And you all just went there?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏂᎪᎯᎸᏲ ᎢᎾ ᏦᏣᏓᏅᏍᎬ Ꮲ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ ᏬᏤᎲ ᏃᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v ahsn nkhilyo in tsotsatanvhskv tlhv utsthin wotsehv nole
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv asn nkilyo in tsotsatanvskv tlv utstin wotsev nole
phrases.english_text: Yeah, but we always moved around, would live in a different place.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᏝᏕ ᏍᎩ ᎤᎾᏭ ᏱᏥᏁᎴ ᎢᏣᏓᏅᏏᏙᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: o lhate ski unaw ytsinle itsa'tnhsitohe
phrases.phonetic_broad: o late ski unaw ytsinle itsatnsitoe
phrases.english_text: Oh so you all just didn’t live there, you all moved around?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ Ꮭ ᎤᎾ ᏲᏥᏁᎴ ᏲᏤᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v lha un yotsinel yotsehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv la un yotsinel yotsee
phrases.english_text: No, we didn’t just live there, or stay there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᏢ ᏕᏣᏕᎳᏆᎡ
phrases.phonetic_text: halv tetsatehlhakwa'e
phrases.phonetic_broad: alv tetsatelakwae

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏅᏲ ᎣᏓᎸ ᏓᏆᏕᎳᏆᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: nvyo otal takwatelakw'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: nvyo otal takwatelakwv
phrases.english_text: I went to school at Rocky Mountain.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏕᏣᏆᏕᏍ ᎤᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: tetskwa'tehs unha
phrases.phonetic_broad: tetskwates una
phrases.english_text: Did you finish there?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᎨᏍᏗ ᏱᏓᎩᏍᏆᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v kehst yitakhskwti
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv kest yitakskwti
phrases.english_text: Uh uh, I didn’t finish.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: lhahs
phrases.phonetic_broad: las
phrases.english_text: No?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᎵᏉᎩᏁᏭ ᏓᏥᏴᎵᏒ ᏣᎩᏑᎸᎪᏨ Ꮎ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎸᎯᏙᎲ Ꮲ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: klhikwoknw tatsi'ylihsv tsakhihsulvkhots na etot tstsihstelvhithv l tulvwhstanehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: klikwoknw tatsiylisv tsakisulvkots na etot tstsistelvitv l tulvwstanev
phrases.english_text: No, I didn’t finish. I was going into the seventh grade and I quit. I started helping my dad where he was working.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏅ ᎠᏛᏁᎮ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏙᏓ ᎢᏨᎵᏍᏕᎵᏙᏗ ᎠᏓᏁᏢᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: tonv atvnhe kehe skina tsatota itsvlhstelhihtohti atanelhvhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tonv atvne kee skina tsatota itsvlstelitoti atanelvskv
phrases.english_text: What did your dad do to provide for you all?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓᏭ Ꮫ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tstalenhvtw t nathvnhv tulvwhihstanehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tstalenvtw t natvnv tulvwistanev
phrases.english_text: He did different things for work.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎯᏍᏕᎵᎮ
phrases.phonetic_text: skin hihstelihe
phrases.phonetic_broad: skin istelie
phrases.english_text: And you were helping him?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭵ ᏚᏯ ᏱᎩ ᏙᏣᏕᏍᎬ ᎠᏂᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏅᏱᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏙᏍᏚᏖᏍᎪ Ꮲ ᏳᏚᎸ ᎩᎶ ᏠᎨᏏ ᎦᏅᎦᎸᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏙᏥᏏᎵᏛᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: v thuya yk totsatehskv anile yk nvyle yk tohstuthehsko tlhv ytulv khilo lokehs kanvklti nle totsihsiltvhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: v tuya yk totsateskv anile yk nvyle yk tostutesko tlv ytulv kilo lokes kanvklti nle totsisiltvskv
phrases.english_text: Yes, we would pick beans or strawberries. Or we would pick up rocks if someone wanted a field cleaned up, or we would build fences.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮭ ᏯᏅᏓᏗ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎾᏈᏱᎲ ᎠᏂ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎢᏣᏕᏍᎬ ᏥᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: lha yhantati ika ankwhiyihv an nahiyu itsatehsk tsiki
phrases.phonetic_broad: la yantati ika ankwiyiv an naiyu itsatesk tsiki
phrases.english_text: Do you remember how much they were paying for strawberries back then when you all were picking them?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎪᎯ ᏯᏓᏅᏙᏭᎴ ᏱᎩ ᎨᎵ
phrases.phonetic_text: skohi ytantwle yk keli
phrases.phonetic_broad: skoi ytantwle yk keli
phrases.english_text: I think it was 10 cents.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎪᎯ ᏯᏓᏅᏙᏭᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: skhi ytantwhs
phrases.phonetic_broad: ski ytantws
phrases.english_text: Just 10 cents?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv
phrases.english_text: Yeah.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏎᏃ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮎ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᏃᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎦ ᏲᏝ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎣᏝ
phrases.phonetic_text: ahsen nahiy n tsikhsv unohsti ohsta ika yothl kehv atela olha
phrases.phonetic_broad: asen naiy n tsiksv unosti osta ika yotl kev atela ola
phrases.english_text: But back then, with a dollar, you had quite a bit of money.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎦ ᏲᏝ ᏲᏩ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎯᎢᏃ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ ᏲᏄᎸᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohsta ik yol yowha khehv kohuhst hi'ino khohiy tsik yonlvnhv

phrases.english_text: I worked for a year on the railroad in ‘71. Then I worked in Tulsa, where those boys were working at that Ford place, for a year too. phrases.english_text: One time at Rocky Mountain, to the south, my grandfather lived on a hill. Me and the boys were walking in the field. I don’t know if it was coons or something was crawling around on there, it was clean. It was just smooth. “Y’all get away,,” the boy said. “Let’s leave!”, he said. We went just a little ways, and an old lady screamed. She said, “Hey where did you boys go? You all come back,” she said.

phrases.english_text: Yeah. When that bean picker [truck] started coming, it was coming just right. The pickers are this big [gestures] and the belt is laying here. It went like this, and made a sound. That boy, that was driving, quickly screamed, “There is a snake,” he said. “Wait,” I said, “Give it a little more gas.” He pushed the feet, it went good. The snake just fell perfectly in there, where the belt was. Then it went perfectly over the dumpster. And he was pulling the dumpster where the beans fell in. And it fell in there—it was rattling hard. That Mexican came and said, “What are you going to do with it?” I said, “I don’t know. What are you going to do with it?” I told him. He went, got a gun from the pickup. He was running. He killed that snake right there. That bean picker was running, it was idling. I dumped the dumpster. It [the snake] fell on the ground. That Mexican picked it up and put it in the pickup. He took it to the end of the fence he was over there digging. And he buried it. He dug a pretty long hole, he put it in there. It was dangerous to pick beans. Since they started, they would pick some up this long [gestures]. The one that was driving that big truck, was holding a pitchfork. He said, “Get up there and level those beans.” As for me, I don’t think so. ”It’s your truck, you do it,” I told him.

phrases.english_text: I did like things like that—working outside. I seen something funny, or it really wasn’t funny. It rained a lot when we were staying in Alabama. Beans-- We didn’t pick that morning, it was raining. I told them boys “We better go look at them bean pickers.” So we got in the truck and left. There was kind of a draw where water flows by. That water was flowing hard. They had beans planted on this side. Them Black men had clubs this long [gesture] what do they call them? Eel, they were killing. That kind. They were clubbing them.
